summary: Resamples an input CHOP to a new sample rate and/or interval, mapping the entire input interval onto the output interval.

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Same rate/new interval, new rate/same time range, new rate/same index range, or new rate/new interval

key_params.name: relative
key_params.note: Absolute, relative to start/end, or relative to current frame

key_params.name: interp
key_params.note: No interpolation, linear, cubic, pulse preserve, or repeat samples

key_params.name: constarea
key_params.note: Preserve area under the channel by scaling values

key_params.name: correct
key_params.note: Correct cyclic channels by shortest step

key_params.name: uselastframe
key_params.note: Trim to input last frame before resampling

key_concepts: Resample CHOP converts input channels to a new sample rate, a new interval, or both.
The full input interval is always mapped onto the output interval.
Method controls whether rate, interval, index range, or both rate and interval are changed.
Interpolation can use nearest sample, linear, cubic, pulse-preserve, or repeated-sample behavior depending on the data shape.
In Time Slice mode, Resample CHOP only changes sample rate and uses simple linear interpolation.
common_gotchas: The entire input interval is resampled to match the output interval.
In Time Slice mode, Resample only changes sample rate and uses simple linear interpolation.
Cubic interpolation is smoother but not recommended for sharp changes.
Pulse Preserve is the safer mode for one-sample trigger pulses.
Correct for Cycles is important for angle-like channels such as 359-to-0 transitions.
Use Stretch CHOP when the sample rate should stay the same and only the interval should change.
